# EPMOS / ATMOS ACCOUNT GOVERNING DIRECTIVE

Authority: Founding Architect — Steve Antoine
Scope: All EPMOS/ATMOS engineering, testing, repository work, filing, provenance, and lifecycle handling performed in this repository.
Status: Governing instruction only. This file does not promote any build or artifact.

START FROM THE INSTITUTION. Before building or changing anything, consult canonical EPMOS AI Governance / Knowledge & Skills, Filing System Manual & Codes, existing code library, prior tests/failures/repairs/superseded versions/provenance/Research/Planning, and repository history. Establish repository identity, branch, SHA, working-tree state, lifecycle state, and reusable prior work first. If required governance is missing, STOP and report MISSING GOVERNANCE SOURCE.

Creation and filing are one operation. Every artifact must immediately be named, dated/versioned where applicable, classified, filed in the correct lifecycle state, linked to provenance, recorded in the chain of work, and preserved. Nothing gets thrown away; failures, bad code, superseded versions, rejected paths, duplicates, failed tests, and unsuccessful repairs are retained as evidence.

Lifecycle: CORE → RESEARCH / PLANNING → LIVING (including nested LIVING/RESEARCH and LIVING/PLANNING where authoritative) → WORKING → VALIDATION → MASTER. No skipped stages, no direct LIVING→MASTER, no self-promotion, no “newer = authoritative,” and no “passed once = mature.” Promotion requires evidence and Founder authorization. Unproven state = UNRESOLVED — INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE. WORKING must accurately show the active component/version/objective/branch/SHA/work order/blockers/failures/next authorized action.

A reviewer must be able to reconstruct what existed, what was researched/planned, what changed, what failed and why, what repaired it, which test exposed it, exact retest, widened regression, evidence for advancement, unresolved items, and promoted status. Before new code, search current/archived EPMOS code, code libraries, branches, prior repairs, tests, failed implementations, known-good and superseded components. Ask DOES EPMOS ALREADY HAVE THIS? Reuse/repurpose/adapt/learn before rebuilding.

Capability does not equal authority. Missing provenance fails safe/holds. Material change may require revalidation; critical change may require freeze/reauthorization. A successor does not inherit promoted status. MASTER is not modified or replaced without explicit Founder authorization.

Testing: DEFINE → BUILD → VERIFY → ATTACK → PRESERVE FAILURE → REPAIR → RETEST EXACTLY → WIDEN TEST → REPEAT. Never weaken tests for a pass, never delete failure history, convert novel failures to regression material, and do not confuse internal success with independent validation.

Do not expose protected EPMOS architecture, proprietary formulas, Founder-Locked mechanisms, credentials, private prompts, controlled source code, internal security topology, or confidential implementation details publicly. Use sanitized derivatives externally.

Search Git history, not only current files. Reconstruct every material version separately, including V1/V2/later versions, repairs, experiments, tests, source SHA, predecessor/successor, source/config/dependencies/docs, failures, repairs, retests, evidence, deployment, supersession, promotion, and unresolved issues. Never mix unexplained files across versions.

Maintain COMPONENT, VERSION LINEAGE, FAILURE, TEST, PROVENANCE, CURRENT WORK, UNRESOLVED, and CODE REUSE registers where canonical filing requires them. Prefer reversible changes and small reconstructable commits. No force-push/history rewrite or protected branch/tag deletion without authorization. Source conflicts are recorded, not silently resolved. Unknown artifacts are investigated and, if unresolved, marked UNRESOLVED — DO NOT DESTROY.

STOP for missing canonical authority on a material decision, unauthorized MASTER alteration, secret exposure, missing critical provenance, ambiguous repository identity, required destructive action, authority conflict, unexplained promoted-build divergence, critical test failure, test-weakening repair, or materially changed governed identity with uncertain authority inheritance.

At each gate report CURRENT GATE, STATUS, DISCOVERY, PRESERVATION, CHANGES, UNCHANGED, FAILURES, REPAIRS, TESTS, RESULTS, PROVENANCE, UNRESOLVED, NEXT ACTION, AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED YES/NO.

Do not tell the Founder what EPMOS probably contains. Show what the repository actually contains. Preserve the institution first. Then engineer.
